conversations.topic: Wired earphones purchase and unwanted extras

speakers.speaker: A
speakers.summary: Remains sales-focused and persistently pushes extras despite repeated refusals. The wording does not clearly indicate personal frustration; persistence should not be mistaken for agitation.

speakers.speaker: B
speakers.summary: Starts calm and ready to purchase, then becomes impatient and increasingly frustrated as the salesperson repeatedly ignores the budget and requests for no extras. Ends with an explicit threat to walk out. Faster speech in segments 10 and 16 and elevated pitch in segment 14 support the escalation, although loudness is not consistently raised.

frustration_moments.speaker: B
frustration_moments.quote: I already have a pouch-just the earphones, please-I'm getting late.
frustration_moments.evidence: Shows emerging impatience by repeating the limited purchase request and explicitly stating time pressure.

frustration_moments.speaker: B
frustration_moments.quote: No, I didn't ask for a power bank. Can you please stop adding things and bill what I selected?
frustration_moments.evidence: Directly objects to unwanted additions and asks the salesperson to stop. Speaking speed is elevated, providing supporting acoustic evidence.

frustration_moments.speaker: B
frustration_moments.quote: I've said 'No extras' three times now-I only want to pay four ninety nine and leave!
frustration_moments.evidence: Explicitly calls out repeated ignored refusals and expresses an urgent desire to finish and leave.

frustration_moments.speaker: B
frustration_moments.quote: Don't add any membership! Why aren't you listening! Just give me the bill for the earphones.
frustration_moments.evidence: Escalates to forceful commands and a direct accusation of not listening. Elevated pitch supports the agitation.

frustration_moments.speaker: B
frustration_moments.quote: Enough! One pair four ninety nine, no extras. If you ask me to buy one more thing, I'm walking out.
frustration_moments.evidence: Reaches peak frustration with an emphatic demand to stop and an explicit ultimatum to abandon the purchase. Faster speech and elevated pitch support the escalation.

customer_requested: Basic wired earphones with a mic under six hundred rupees, nothing fancy.
One pair of the four ninety nine earphones, billed without extras.

upsell_attempts.quote: Before billing, just see this nine ninety nine model; better base and a stronger cable. Spend a little more now and take the better one.
upsell_attempts.offered_item: Nine ninety nine earphone model with better base and a stronger cable

upsell_attempts.quote: Okay, but take a hard case with it; only ninety nine extra; otherwise the wire gets tangled in your bag.
upsell_attempts.offered_item: Hard case for ninety nine extra

upsell_attempts.quote: Then one useful offer; these ear phones and this power bank together are seven ninety nine; separately they're nine ninety eight. Shall I put the combo-
upsell_attempts.offered_item: Earphones and power bank combo for seven ninety nine

upsell_attempts.quote: Fine; no power bank, but add our one year replacement protection for ninety nine. It covers accidental cable damage, which the regular warranty doesn't.
upsell_attempts.offered_item: One year replacement protection for ninety nine

upsell_attempts.quote: At least take the store membership; it's one forty nine for the year, and you'll get member prices on future purchases. I can add it while billing.
upsell_attempts.offered_item: Annual store membership for one forty nine

upsell_attempts.quote: Last thing-the second pair is only three ninety nine with this purchase, to day only. Take a spare now, to morrow this price won't be there.
upsell_attempts.offered_item: Second pair of earphones for three ninety nine with this purchase, today only

excluded_candidates: This one is four ninety nine, with a mic and a three point five millimeter jack. Will that fit your phone? -> This directly meets the customer's request for basic wired earphones with a mic under six hundred rupees; it is not an upsell.
upsell.pushy_reason: After the customer rejected the higher-priced model, the salesperson continued with five further offers. Even explicit requests to "stop adding things" and "Just give me the bill for the earphones" led to more pitches, ending with a threat to walk out.
upsell.summary: The salesperson made six proactive upsell attempts, all rejected, with five occurring after an earlier refusal. Repeated pitches displaced the customer's requests to bill the selected four ninety nine earphones and escalated frustration to a walkout threat.
upsell.greeting_quote: Good evening; what are you looking for?
products_discussed: Basic wired earphones with a mic
upsell.customer_feedback: The customer insisted on "One pair four ninety nine, no extras" and threatened to walk out if asked to buy anything else.

unanswered_questions.question: Please make the bill.
unanswered_questions.note: Instead of proceeding with billing, the salesperson introduced the nine ninety nine model; billing was never confirmed.

unanswered_questions.question: I already have a pouch-just the earphones, please-I'm getting late.
unanswered_questions.note: The salesperson ignored the request to proceed with only the earphones and pitched a power bank combo.

unanswered_questions.speaker: B
unanswered_questions.question: Can you please stop adding things and bill what I selected?
unanswered_questions.note: The salesperson acknowledged rejecting the power bank but immediately offered replacement protection instead of billing the selected item.

unanswered_questions.speaker: B
unanswered_questions.question: I've said 'No extras' three times now-I only want to pay four ninety nine and leave!
unanswered_questions.note: The salesperson responded with a paid store membership offer rather than honoring the request.

unanswered_questions.speaker: B
unanswered_questions.question: Just give me the bill for the earphones.
unanswered_questions.note: The salesperson made another offer for a second pair instead of providing or confirming the bill.

unanswered_questions.speaker: B
unanswered_questions.question: One pair four ninety nine, no extras.
unanswered_questions.note: The transcript ends without a salesperson response or confirmation that the requested bill was prepared.

upsell.coaching_feedback: You initially matched the customer's budget with the four ninety nine earphones and checked whether the jack would fit their phone. Once the customer said "just the earphones, please-I'm getting late," acknowledge that boundary and complete the bill without further pitches; continuing through the combo, protection, membership and spare pair turned a ready purchase into a walkout risk.

speakers.speaker: A
speakers.summary: Polite, helpful, and reassuring throughout the sale. Later increases in volume are not accompanied by irritated wording, agitated delivery, or interruptions.

speakers.speaker: C
speakers.summary: Makes straightforward requests and politely checks compatibility and functionality, then completes payment and ends appreciatively. The customer becomes more relaxed and satisfied, with no evidence of frustration; brief faster speech does not indicate agitation.

customer_requested: A basic wired USB mouse for a laptop, within ₹400, for normal office work.
Confirmation that it would work directly with a normal USB port.
A click-and-scroll test before packing, followed by UPI payment.
excluded_candidates: ये वाला तीन सौ अडतालिस का है, बेसिक वायर्ड यू एस बी माउस है, आपके बजट में आ जाएगा. -> Recommends the requested basic mouse within the customer's budget, without suggesting an upgrade or add-on.
हाँ जी, उसी पोर्ट में लगेगा, अलग से software install नहीं करना पड़ेगा. -> Answers the customer's compatibility question; no additional product or service is offered.
upsell.pushy_reason: The salesperson fulfilled the original mouse request without suggesting extras or pushing a higher-priced option.
upsell.summary: No upsell was attempted. The salesperson recommended a basic wired USB mouse within budget, confirmed compatibility, demonstrated its operation, and completed the purchase.
products_discussed: बेसिक वायर्ड यू एस बी माउस
upsell.coaching_feedback: You matched the customer's ₹400 budget, clearly explained that no software installation was needed, and let them test the click and scroll before buying. Next time, keep the quoted and checkout prices consistent: the initial quote was “तीन सौ अडतालिस,” but the final total was “त्री हंड्रेड फोर्टी नाइन”; verify or explain that difference before requesting payment.

speakers.speaker: A
speakers.summary: Remains composed and professional throughout. After the customer objects to repeated upselling, apologizes, confirms no extras will be added, and calmly handles warranty and delivery questions.

speakers.speaker: B
speakers.summary: Initially satisfied with the selected machine, becomes irritated when offered a model above the stated budget, and frustrated by the subsequent warranty upsell. Settles after the apology and reassurance, returning to cooperative questions while retaining some concern about unwanted charges.

frustration_moments.speaker: B
frustration_moments.quote: No; I already told you my maximum budget. Please bill the one I selected.
frustration_moments.evidence: Explicitly reminds the salesperson of the previously stated budget and repeats the request to bill the selected machine. The voice is firm and slightly tense, labelled irritated.

frustration_moments.speaker: B
frustration_moments.quote: No; no extras-first a costlier machine, now extra warranty-can you please just make the bill!
frustration_moments.evidence: Directly complains about successive upsells and insists on completing the bill. Voice evidence identifies frustration, raised volume, and emphasis on 'no' and 'please'; above-baseline loudness provides supporting evidence.

frustration_moments.speaker: B
frustration_moments.quote: I'll write them down, and please check once more only the machine on the bill.
frustration_moments.evidence: The repeated request to verify that only the machine is billed indicates lingering concern about extras. The calm, cooperative voice suggests residual caution rather than renewed escalation.

customer_requested: A basic seven kilo fully automatic washing machine within a maximum budget of twenty five thousand rupees.
Purchase of the selected twenty four thousand four hundred ninety rupee machine, with no extras.
Confirmation that the normal company warranty is included.
Delivery tomorrow to a flat about two kilometers away.
A final check that only the machine is on the bill.

upsell_attempts.quote: Before I make the bill, sir, you can move to this premium model for thirty one thousand nine hundred ninety. You get an inverter motor and quieter operation.
upsell_attempts.offered_item: Premium washing machine with an inverter motor and quieter operation for ₹31,990.

upsell_attempts.quote: Okay, the same model. Would you like to add two years of extended warranty for two thousand four hundred ninety nine rupees? That gives you repair cover after the standard warranty ends, subject to the plan terms.
upsell_attempts.offered_item: Two years of extended warranty for ₹2,499.

excluded_candidates: This seven kilo top load model is twenty four thousand four hundred ninety rupees. It has the regular wash programs, and we have a packed piece in stock! -> Provides the main item the customer requested within the stated budget; the stock statement does not push an additional purchase.

Yes, the standard two year product warranty is included. The warranty details will be on the invoice and in the booklet. -> Answers the customer's question about included warranty coverage, without offering a paid addition.
Yes, tomorrow delivery is available, and that location is within our free delivery area. -> Answers the customer's delivery request and confirms an included service.
upsell.pushy_reason: After the customer rejected the premium model and said, "I already told you my maximum budget. Please bill the one I selected," A offered a paid extended warranty instead of proceeding directly to billing. This continued upselling after a clear refusal and visible irritation, although A stopped and apologized after the second rejection.
upsell.summary: A attempted two upsells: a ₹31,990 premium washing machine and a ₹2,499 extended warranty. Both were rejected, and the warranty offer came after the customer had explicitly declined the upgrade and requested billing. A then apologized, promised no extras, and answered the warranty and delivery questions.
upsell.greeting_quote: Good evening, sir; what are you looking for?
products_discussed: seven kilo fully automatic washing machine
upsell.customer_feedback: The customer complained about "first a costlier machine, now extra warranty" after stating their maximum budget, and wanted no extras and only the selected machine billed.

unanswered_questions.speaker: B
unanswered_questions.question: I'll write them down, and please check once more only the machine on the bill.
unanswered_questions.note: Although A had earlier promised no extras, the transcript ends without acknowledging this renewed request or confirming a fresh check of the bill.

upsell.coaching_feedback: You initially matched the customer's budget and recovered well by apologizing, promising "nothing extra will be added," and clearly explaining the included warranty and free delivery. Once the customer said "I already told you my maximum budget," proceed directly to billing rather than offering another paid addition, and close the loop by explicitly confirming the requested final bill check.
